thread:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER DUTY - High latency + 5xx spike for cross-region requests (us-east1 -> eu-west2). Alert group: cross-region-routing. Triggered at 2025-10-12 03:07:14 UTC. Severity: SEV2

leo_oncall: seeing it. spike in p50/p95 for eu-west2-bound requests from us-east1. customers reporting errors. starting triage.

mariana_sre: logs show a sudden increase in 503s from the routing gateway, and a bunch of requests pinned to eu-west2 backend that should be served from eu-west1 per policy.

ajay_netops: looks like the region-pin service returned stale entries? pulling pin table now.

infra-bot: Deploy log: routing-service v3.8.1 promoted to us-east1 at 02:55 UTC (no errors).

leo_oncall: can someone run a quick dig and curl to confirm DNS and health endpoints?

emily_prodeng: running checks:
```
dig +short service.redwood-route.example A @8.8.8.8
# -> 34.90.12.11  (eu-west2) \n
curl -s -D - https://eu-west2.health.redwood.example/ready -o /dev/null
# -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK\n```

mariana_sre: thanks. but our tracing shows actual requests routed to eu-west2 while policy should steer small percentage there. weight table reads: eu-west1: 90, eu-west2: 10. however the runtime reported weights: eu-west1: 0, eu-west2: 100 for a subset of customers.

chip_support: customer-reported: "Our requests are slower and intermittently failing since ~02:50 UTC" - affected accounts: acme-co, fastship, metrics-ops.

ajay_netops: grabbing router debug. Found a config race: new pin-resolution codepath introduced a fallback that treats unknown latency as 'prefer-nearby' and for nodes in us-east1 that translates to eu-west2 due to stale region coordinates.

leo_oncall: temporary mitigation idea: flip routing fallback to strict weight enforcement and flush prefix KV cache so we force re-eval. Can someone run the command?

mariana_sre: I'm going to push a targeted flag to routing-service to ignore the fallback for 30m. Doing canary to 10% first.

emily_prodeng: tagging for rollback plan: if errors increase, revert flag -> `routing.fallback_mode = \"legacy-weighted\"`

mariana_sre: rollout commands:
```
# set feature flag (k8s) for routing-service
kubectl -n routing set env deploy/routing-service ROUTING_FALLBACK=legacy-weighted --record
# flush prefix KV cache
curl -X POST "https://ops-api.redwood.example/kv/flush?prefix=pin-resolve" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${OPSTOKEN}"
```

infra-bot: Feature flag rollout started (10% -> 02:26 UTC).

leo_oncall: flushing caches now.

ajay_netops: dig shows TTLs are low (60s) so DNS won't be the long pole. This is internal policy mis-eval, not public DNS.

chip_support: updating customers: sending note to acme-co and fastship that we're investigating routing and applying mitigation.

mariana_sre: can we also pin a manual override for these three customers to eu-west1 until stable? we have selector-based overrides.

leo_oncall: yes. applying per-customer override: `route.override[acme-co] = eu-west1` etc.

emily_prodeng: applied overrides for acme-co and fastship. verifying traffic now.

infra-bot: Override applied for acme-co, fastship, metrics-ops at 03:11:40 UTC.

mariana_sre: p95 latency is dropping for overridden customers. global error rate falling ~70% since cache flush + flag.

leo_oncall: still seeing a tail for non-overridden customers. continuing ramp of flag to 50% to capture more nodes.

ajay_netops: quick note: the pin-resolution service had an edge-case where metadata TTL from datastore could be read as 0 if a previous write was partial. That caused the runtime to treat the entry as "unknown" and fall back. we'll need a fix to treat 0 as stale, not as present.

mariana_sre: bug filed: INF-4823 "pin-resolution: treat zero TTL as stale". assigned to ajay.

chip_support: customers who saw errors: acme-co (partial), fastship (partial), metrics-ops (errors + timeouts). CS outreach in progress.

leo_oncall: ETA on code fix?

ajay_netops: I can ship a safe patch to pin-resolution that forces TTL>=30s on read in ~30m, will require a rolling restart of pin-resolver in us-east1. Doing it after we get mitigation stable.

mariana_sre: good. timeline: 03:08 alert -> 03:12 mitigations (cache flush + overrides) -> 03:20 noticeable improvement. moving to monitoring -> watch for 1 hour, then decide on severity and postmortem.

pagerduty-bot: Incident updated: Severity remains SEV2. Current status: stabilizing. Notes: targeted overrides applied; feature flag rollout at 50%; patch INF-4823 created.

emily_prodeng: quick customer-impact summary for postmortem: ~4% of cross-region traffic misrouted during 02:50-03:20 UTC, peak error rate 4.8% for affected prefixes, three paying customers had visible failures. No data loss. Estimated cost impact minimal.

leo_oncall: handing off to mariana for ongoing watch. I'll go offline in 5.

mariana_sre: taking oncall. will keep this thread updated every 15m. if errors re-spike, page me.

chip_support: sending final customer updates, will collect any extra logs from acme-co.

mariana_sre: next steps checklist:
- [ ] roll pin-resolver patch (INF-4823) and monitor
- [ ] add additional unit/integration tests for zero TTL case
- [ ] run a controlled canary of new pin-resolution logic in us-east1
- [ ] prepare postmortem draft (impact, root cause, mitigation, timeline)

leo_oncall: +1 on timeline. thanks all. :thumbsup:

mariana_sre: marking incident as transitioning to 'watch' at 03:20 UTC. will reopen if metrics deteriorate.
